main_text.p: mandarant, ij nimirum qui ( non secus ac Timotheus ac Titus ) succedebant in ordinariam poteftatem in ampliori aliqua parte Ecclefiæ & jam plures Presbyteros complectente.

Ea vero humilitate erant Primi Illi Episcopi, ut declinantes eximium Apostolorum nomen (quod jam ftylus Ecclefiæ à communi illa fua acceptione (qua Nuncium vel Missum significat) ad specialem Illam dignitatem traduxerat, quæ Extraordinariam suam Vocationem, Missionem, Dona & Potestatem immediate à Christo acceperat) fat haberent fe Episcopos vel Presbyteros vocari; donec tandem consuetudo (magna verborum arbitratrix & loquendi norma) cum justa causa videretur peculiari aliquo Nomine distinguendi quorum Jus & officium in Ecclesia non diversum solum à cæteris, sed Illis omnibus erat superius (cum Apostolorum essent succedanei in Ordinaria illa & perpetua potestate administrandi Ecclesias, utcunque Nominis Illius Honore, modestè sed laudabili more abstinentes) his Nomen Episcopi appropriandum vellet: quod fanè fieri potuit absque ulla vel minima Arrogantiæ nota in Eos, qui propagine quadam Apostolica recta serie ab illis descendentes, excelsissima & Amplissima Potestate in duebantur gubernandi puriffimas & Primitivas Ecclesias, quæ proculdubio multos habebant sanctos Episcopos ad exemplum Titi & Timothei, quorum peculiaris potestas haud magis clare innotescit ex præfatis Epi-stolis,

page.notes: Printed "ij" in line 1 kept as printed. Catchword "stolis," is the continuation of "Epistolis," split at the line end. Running head Greek kept as printed (EIKΩN BAΣIAIKH.). Page number read as 150 from a decorative numeral; [?] would apply if doubtful. Italic extent on a few words (Missum, diversum, superius, succedanei) read from type shape and may need checking. Two printed lines in the middle of the text were close to illegible at the right edge of the scan, but readable on inspection.
